title: Glue a broken mug handle back on: dry-fit it, squeeze a thin bead onto each broken face, seat and press
instruction: A stoneware mug whose handle has broken off lies on its side in a foam cradle, the two broken stubs on its side facing up. The handle, in one piece, stands on its two broken ends on a felt pad. A tube of no-drip gel glue (LePage Extreme Glue No Drip Gel) stands nozzle down in its holder, its cap off. Glue the handle back on as the glue's maker directs: first dry-fit it (seat both broken ends on their stubs at once, then lift it off and stand it back on its two ends on the pad); then squeeze a thin bead from the tube onto each stub's broken face, keeping glue off everything else; put the tube back in its holder before you seat the handle; and within 5 minutes of the first glue (the maker's limit) seat both ends of the handle on their stubs at once, flush, press it down firmly on both and let go, leaving the mug and the handle undisturbed in the cradle.
context: A common home repair: LePage's ceramics guide says "If the mug has simply cracked in half or the handle has fallen off, you can follow the steps above" and names Extreme Glue No Drip Gel as "rated safe for items that hold hot liquids". The glue's technical data sheet (Henkel, LePage Extreme Glue No Drip Gel, a "Squeeze Tube" of "20 g") gives the order followed here (masking, dampening and closing the tube are not scored): "Pre-fit all materials before applying adhesive"; "Mask off the adjacent areas with tape before gluing if necessary"; "Apply thin layer of adhesive to one surface. Immediately position and press parts firmly together within 5 minutes"; "Do not move or use parts for at least 2 hours"; Open Time "3-5 minutes". The mug is sized from the IKEA DINERA (stoneware, Height "9 cm", "30 cl"; its radius is derived, not listed). The skill: meter a bead from a squeeze tube onto a small face, keep the glaze clean, then mate and press two ends at once.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table top. The demo uses the right arm; either arm may be used (both are watched). Fixed: a foam cradle of two rails (inner edges 22 mm either side of x 0.245, 15 mm high, 160 mm long along y); a felt pad (90 mm square) at (0.19, -0.215); a tube holder (35 mm high, a 16 mm square well) at (0.3, -0.215). Loose: a stoneware mug (78 mm across, 90 mm long, 280 g) lying in the cradle, its axis along y at y -0.095 (layout 0), its mouth toward +y, two broken stubs on top 55 mm apart, each a 12 by 8 mm biscuit-coloured face 3 mm proud of the glaze, each on a stiff spring (2.5 N/mm, 1 N preload) that measures the press on it; the handle (25 g), an arch 27 mm high with its 12 by 8 mm broken ends 55 mm apart, standing on its ends on the pad; a 30 g tube (20 g of gel) standing nozzle down in its holder, cap off, its two walls 22 mm apart, each sliding in up to 6 mm against a spring (2 N/mm, 1 N preload). Gel leaves the nozzle only while the walls' mean squeeze is over 4 N, at 2.5 uL/s per N of it over that, and lands where the nozzle points. By seed (layout 0: handle shifted (0, 0) mm and turned 0 deg, mug shifted 0 mm along y; layout 1: handle shifted (12, -10) mm and turned 20 deg, mug shifted 20 mm along y; layout 2: handle shifted (-10, 12) mm and turned -17 deg, mug shifted -18 mm along y). The broken faces are clean and dry (prep out of scope).
scoring: Glue lands on a broken face when the nozzle's tip is over it (at least 1.5 mm inside its edges, up to 4 mm above, or resting on it) and points down within 20 deg; otherwise it is astray. A thin bead is 10 to 30 uL on a face. An end is seated when it is centred within 1.5 mm of its face across and along the mug and every corner of it 0.3 mm into to 0.6 mm over the face in height, the handle square to the mug within 4 deg. Dry fit: both ends seated at once, then the handle standing on its ends on the pad (its centre 35 mm or less from the pad's centre each way, within 3 mm of its start height, upright within 10 deg) with both hands clear, before any glue. Joined: both ends seated on thin beads with the tube back in its holder, within 300 s of the first glue; lifted off before let go (an end over 2 mm up, or its centre over 1.5 mm from its face's centre), it must be seated and pressed again. Pressed: then both stubs at 3 N or more at once for 0.5 s. Clear: each hand open (each finger 3 mm off the part) and its TCP 30 mm off, or 100 mm off. Success (1.0, held 1 s): pressed, both hands clear, the handle still (under 10 mm/s) and unmoved in the mug's frame since let go, the tube back in its holder (within 10 mm across and 6 mm in height, upright within 10 deg), the mug in the cradle. Partial credit at the last step: all that but not yet held 1 s 0.8; joined 0.6; dry-fitted and both beads 0.4; dry-fitted 0.2. Scored 0 from then on: glue before the dry fit or before the handle is back on the pad, the handle seated on glue before the tube is back, over 1 uL astray, an end seated on more than 30 uL (squeezed out), the handle moved over 1 mm after it was let go on its glue, the mug over 8 mm out of place or turned over 5 deg, a part 30 mm below the table top, or the glue model not running.
reset_notes: The mug in its cradle and the handle on its pad by seed; the tube in its holder, unsqueezed; no glue anywhere. Nothing else moves.
fidelity: Approximate. PhysX has no fluids or soft tubes: the tube is two sprung walls; the gel's flow, where it lands and the bead are our model (the bead is drawn pale and 8 to 14 times a real layer's thickness so it shows). The stubs are sprung only to measure the press. The mug collides as a 32-sided prism, its centre of mass 3 mm below its axis for the foam's grip. The glue has no strength. The 150 s run never reaches the open time or the 2 h hold. Handle and stub sizes are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (3,000 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 74.2 s, step 1,484)
